chapter.title: There, Their, and They're
chapter.description: Master the differences between the homophones 'there', 'their', and 'they're' to ensure accurate word choice in writing.

rules.title: There (Location or Existence)
rules.explanation: Use 'there' to refer to a place or location, or to state that something exists (e.g., 'there is' or 'there are'). Think of the word 'here' inside 'there'.
rules.example: Please put the box over there. / There are three apples on the table.

rules.title: Their (Possession)
rules.explanation: Use 'their' as a possessive pronoun showing that something belongs to two or more people or things. Think of the word 'heir' inside 'their'.
rules.example: The students finished their homework. / The trees lost their leaves.

rules.title: They're (Contraction)
rules.explanation: Use 'they're' only as a contraction for 'they are'. If you cannot substitute 'they are' into the sentence, 'they're' is incorrect.
rules.example: They're going to the park. (= They are going to the park.)

questions.sentence: The children are playing with ________ toys in the garden.
questions.explanation: 'Their' indicates that the toys belong to the children.

questions.sentence: Look over ________! Is that a rainbow?
questions.explanation: 'There' refers to a specific place or location.

questions.sentence: ________ going to be late for the flight if they don't hurry.
questions.explanation: 'They're' is the contraction for 'they are' ('They are going to be late').

questions.sentence: ________ are many reasons why people love living in this city.
questions.explanation: 'There' is used to state existence ('There are many reasons').

questions.sentence: The smiths parked ________ car in front of the driveway.
questions.explanation: 'Their' is possessive, showing ownership of the car.

exercises.title: Their vs. There vs. They're Quiz

questions.question: Choose the sentence in which words are used correctly.
options: They're going to pick up their suits over there.
Their going to pick up they're suits over there.
questions.answer: They're going to pick up their suits over there.
questions.explanation: 'They're' = they are; 'their' = possessive suits; 'there' = location.

questions.question: Choose the sentence in which words are used correctly.
options: Is there any chance they're bringing their dog?
Is their any chance there bringing they're dog?
questions.answer: Is there any chance they're bringing their dog?
questions.explanation: 'There' indicates existence, 'they're' = they are, and 'their' shows dog ownership.

questions.question: Choose the sentence in which words are used correctly.
options: The house standing over there lost its roof during the storm.
The house standing over their lost it's roof during the storm.
questions.answer: The house standing over there lost its roof during the storm.
questions.explanation: 'There' refers to the location of the house.

questions.question: Choose the sentence in which words are used correctly.
options: They're not sure if their tickets are valid for the event.
There not sure if they're tickets are valid for the event.
questions.answer: They're not sure if their tickets are valid for the event.
questions.explanation: 'They're' = they are; 'their' shows possession of tickets.

questions.question: Choose the sentence in which words are used correctly.
options: There were three books lying on their desk.
They're were three books lying on there desk.
questions.answer: There were three books lying on their desk.
questions.explanation: 'There' introduces existence; 'their' indicates ownership of the desk.

questions.sentence: The birds built ________ nest in the high oak tree.
questions.explanation: 'Their' is the possessive pronoun referring to the birds.

questions.sentence: ________ always friendly when we meet them in the hallway.
questions.explanation: 'They're' stands for 'they are'.

questions.sentence: Wait ________ while I call a taxi.
questions.explanation: 'There' refers to a location.

questions.sentence: Both students forgot ________ backpacks on the bus.
questions.explanation: 'Their' is possessive.

questions.sentence: ________ planning to visit France this summer.
questions.explanation: 'They're' is the contraction for 'they are'.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: The players held ____ trophies high in the air.
questions.explanation: 'Their' shows possession of the trophies by the players.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: ____ isn't any milk left in the refrigerator.
questions.explanation: 'There' indicates the non-existence of milk.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: I hope ____ having a great time on vacation.
questions.explanation: Contraction for 'they are'.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: Put the bags right ____ by the door.
questions.explanation: Refers to a specific place.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: The cats were washing ____ fur in the sun.
questions.explanation: Possessive form for plural animals.
